openings.claim: Contact boundaries guide the plate; slack wire tethers the removable gate to the carriage for recoverability, neither attaching to nor locating the plate. Use four strips: two side boundaries, backstop, removable gate; cork pads, drilled strips, existing slots and supplied bolts. Rival: identical guide geometry, wire on a removable plate sling, gate untethered. Guided and tethered components differ.
openings.discriminator: If feasible, both may retain equally; candidate permits complete plate separation while recovering its gate, rival keeps plate connected. Faster glove handling from wire not following the plate is speculative; equal/slower service defeats that advantage. Gate escape, tether slip, excess movement/time or forbidden contact defeats the candidate.
openings.probe: Dry-fit both first. Reject layouts violating: no drilling/cutting/heating/gluing plate or carriage; expose marked 30 mm edge; no added part in stroke clearance; carriage remains on rails. Within eighty fabrication and twenty observation minutes, compare at most two configurations, three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each. Final run uses spare; final service check uses thick gloves. Record displacement, time, edge contact, wire interference, recoverability. Require every candidate run within 1 mm and every service check within sixty seconds without touching the marked edge. Stop if resources cannot accommodate both; a stop cap proves no feasibility.
openings.uncertainty: Slot dimensions, accessible fastening surfaces, strip bendability and clearance permitting a positive gate with six bolts are unprovided. Both wire attachments must be removable/recoverable without forbidden alteration or intrusion; failure prevents comparison. Mechanical retention avoids assuming stronger spare magnet holding: supplied pull check 3 N versus 7 N. Proposed interface scramble only; no demonstrated build, performance or additional permission.

lineage.reason: Retains relation, rival, conditional predictions, defeats, resource stop, unknowns and declared uncertain fit.

decision: Dry-fit before comparison; proceed only if geometry, fastening and resource envelope permit both arrangements.
